idea-plugin.name: Sandbox Agent Connector
idea-plugin.description:
Sandbox Agent Connector lets you pair-program with an AI coding agent that runs inside an isolated sandbox (Docker Sandboxes sbx, Docker, Apple Container or WSL Containers), while your IDE stays lightweight on the host. Only agent execution, file editing and tool invocation are offloaded to the sandbox — you keep the native editor, diff viewer, navigation and debugger.

The plugin talks to the agent over stdio using the Agent Client Protocol (ACP v1), a JSON-RPC 2.0 based protocol, so any ACP-compatible agent (for example the Claude Code ACP adapter) can be used.

Highlights

  • Sandbox isolation – the agent reads, writes and runs commands only inside the sandbox, so your local environment and secrets are never touched by accident. The plugin advertises no client-side file system (read or write) or terminal capability. Credentials such as API keys are never forwarded from the IDE: they have to be present in the sandbox already.
  • Inline approval – every file change or command execution requested through session/request_permission appears as a permission card in the tool window, with a compact diff, a link to the native full diff viewer, and the exact command to be run.
  • IDE-native chat UI – Markdown streaming, collapsible thinking log, tool-call cards with live status, plan cards, interactive task-list choices, slash commands and token usage. The transcript is rendered in an embedded browser (JCEF), with syntax highlighting by the IDE lexers; Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a newline (rebindable in the IDE keymap).
  • Explicit context control – the active file, the selection and manually attached files are shown as removable chips above the prompt, so you always see what is sent to the model. Auto-attach is off by default.
  • Session history – sessions can be listed, switched, renamed and deleted; transcripts are snapshotted locally and restored via session/load / session/resume. Each row of the list tells at a glance whether the session is stored locally and has backups.
  • Local session protection – the local transcript is never lost to the agent: a session with local history is drawn from it, and when the history the agent replays differs in its agent messages (compared by their ACP message ids), the local transcript is kept as a backup before the agent's version replaces it; deleting a session moves its transcript and its backups aside instead of erasing them. Backups and deleted sessions open in a Read Only tab that never connects to the sandbox.
  • Local session search – Search Local Sessions in the tool window options menu searches the full text of every locally stored session, its backups and, on request, deleted ones. The matching part is previewed as pretty printed JSON with the match highlighted; a result reopens the session or opens it in a Read Only tab.
  • Safe turns – in-memory documents are flushed before a turn, the workspace is optionally locked read-only in the IDE while the agent works, and changed paths are refreshed in the VFS afterwards.
  • Sandbox terminal – Open Sandbox Terminal logs into the very same sandbox in a terminal tab of the IDE; it needs the bundled Terminal plugin to be enabled.
  • Auditable traffic – all JSON-RPC lines exchanged with the agent are written to a per-session log file under the IDE log directory.

Getting started

  1. Start a sandbox that mounts your project root read-write (for example sbx).
  2. Configure the sandbox type, the sandbox name, the ACP agent (picked from the ACP registry) and the sandbox workspace under Settings → Tools → Sandbox Agent Connector.
  3. Open the Sandbox Agent tool window, attach to the sandbox and send your first prompt.

The bundled Markdown plugin is a required dependency, and the transcript needs JCEF: where JBCefApp.isSupported() is false, the transcript falls back to plain text and permission requests cannot be answered.

The plugin never starts or stops the sandbox itself; it only attaches to an already running one, so you can keep working with the same container outside the IDE. See the project page for the full specification and installation guide.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • ACP v1 (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio) client that attaches to an agent running in a sandbox (Docker Sandboxes, Docker, Apple Container or WSL Containers).
  • Sandbox Agent tool window: Markdown chat stream, thinking log, tool-call and plan cards, slash commands, token usage and session history (switch / rename / delete).
  • Inline permission cards for file changes (compact diff plus native full diff viewer) and command execution.
  • Context chips for the active file, the selection and manually attached files, with auto-attach off by default.
  • Optional read-only workspace lock during a turn and automatic VFS refresh of sandbox-side changes.
  • Open Sandbox Terminal: a login shell in the same sandbox, opened in a terminal tab of the IDE.
  • Local session protection: a session with local history is drawn from it; a changed agent side history (compared by the agent message ids) backs the local transcript up before replacing it, and deletion moves the transcript and its backups aside. No local file is ever erased.
  • Session list with storage-state icons (local / local with backups / agent only), a full-title tooltip and a hover submenu with Rename / Delete / Backups.
  • Read Only tabs for backups and deleted sessions: no connection, no prompt, transcript search included.
  • Search Local Sessions: full text search over the local sessions (deleted ones optional) with a pretty printed JSON preview of the match.
  • Per-session ACP traffic log under the IDE log directory.
  • Settings page under Tools → Sandbox Agent Connector for the sandbox type and name, the login shell, the ACP agent (from the ACP registry; a binary distribution is started with a command entered by hand), the agent startup idle timeout, the sandbox workspace path, restoring the last session, the read-only workspace lock, context auto-attach and the transcript font size.
